How a well gets drilled here

0–20 ft

Site it

We walk the lot, mark the spot, and check setback lines before the rig moves.

20–180 ft

Drill it

The bit goes down through caliche and sand. Every foot is logged: depth, material, water show.

180–280 ft

Case it

Steel casing drops in, grout seals the annulus, and a sanitary cap keeps surface water out.

280–320 ft

Test it

We measure the water table depth, pump for four hours, and record gallons per minute. You get the numbers in writing.

What we do

  • New water well drilling

    Sited, drilled, cased and tested, with a written drill log of every foot down.

    Price it

  • Well deepening

    When the water table drops below your pump, we go deeper instead of starting over.

    Price it

  • Well pump replacement

    Old pump pulled, new one sized to your depth and set below the summer water level.

    Price it

  • Well pump repair

    Motor, wiring or control box tested at the wellhead so you only pay for what failed.

    Price it

  • Pressure tank service

    Waterlogged tank or a pump that clicks on and off, set back to steady pressure.

    Price it

  • Water level and yield test

    We measure how far down your water sits and how many gallons a minute it gives.

    Price it

  • Water testing

    Lab test for nitrates, fluoride, arsenic and bacteria, explained line by line.

    Price it

  • Well abandonment

    Old or dry wells plugged and sealed to state rules so nothing drains into the aquifer.

    Price it

  • No-water emergency calls

    Taps dry at home? A phone line answered after hours and a truck sent out.

    Price it
